lessons.title: The captain routes. The captain never rows.
I audited my own migrations. It was not fine.
Your thresholds do not belong in constants
Invariants are cheap. Silent corruption is not.
Every filter needs a documented exception
Never silently change a number someone gets paid on
When two sensors disagree, rank them
Your data model is where uncertainty goes to die
One global threshold is how you delete valid data
collectAsState is quietly leaking your work
expect/actual is the wrong default in KMP
Your LazyColumn recomposes on every scroll
The 5-second window that crashes your service
Teaching a phone to disbelieve its own GPS

anthology.title: The Morkinstar Journals
anthology.tagline: Fourteen gods. Fourteen monsters. Thirteen names.

seasons.title: The Directory
seasons.blurb: He files. Ten entries, each a world's legend and the phenomenon it explains.

seasons.title: The Ninety-One Pages
seasons.blurb: He stops filing. Each page must contain something nobody has ever written down.

entries.title: The Legend Of K'öæluæ's Scales
entries.phenomenon: Why it snows for a half momenta every click
entries.blurb: A galactic field reporter transcribes why it snows on a frozen planet — a fire serpent, a water god, and the fisherwoman who talked one of them out of giving up.

entries.title: The Ninety-Nine Names Of Silence
entries.phenomenon: The Ösk, a half-momenta every click in which nobody speaks aloud
entries.blurb: On the coldest world in Alpha Axmoiri, everything has ninety-nine names, and once a click ninety-eight of them are gone. A deaf child, a god with no name of his own, and the invention of writing as an act of war.

entries.title: The Tide That Owes
entries.phenomenon: The Withdrawal, nine days a click in which the sea leaves and does not come back
entries.blurb: A queen borrowed nine days of ocean to end a famine. Nobody wrote down the terms. Four thousand clicks later, the sea is still collecting.

entries.title: The Word Marltains Do Not Have
entries.phenomenon: Marltains are born in pairs and have no word for being alone
entries.blurb: The Directory logged the Marltain binary wrong, and I repeated the error. Here is the correction, and the story of the first Marltain to be one.

entries.title: The Arm Shake
entries.phenomenon: Killugans embrace strangers on meeting, and hold for a count of eleven
entries.blurb: I made a joke about this system in Entry #2245. Then I came here and found out that the hug is not a greeting. It is a test, it has been running for four thousand clicks, and it has never been switched off.

entries.title: The Standing Dead
entries.phenomenon: The dead are buried standing, and every grave on the planet faces the same fixed celestial bearing
entries.blurb: On Jötunheimr the dead do not lie down. They are surveyed, aimed, and set into a line four thousand clicks long, and the line is still being extended, and I made the mistake of asking what it points at.

entries.title: The Kindling
entries.phenomenon: Every ninth generation the Væhn destroy their complete written record, on purpose, entirely
entries.blurb: Every ninth generation, an entire civilisation burns everything it has ever written. They keep one page. A child writes it. I read the oldest one and then I did something I have never done in 2284 entries.

entries.title: Two Suns, One Shadow
entries.phenomenon: Two stars in the sky, and every object on the surface casts exactly one shadow
entries.blurb: On Solvei the word for god and the word for monster are the same word, inflected by which way you are standing. I went to file a linguistic curiosity. I came back with an arithmetic problem.

entries.title: The World With No Number
entries.phenomenon: None. That is the phenomenon.
entries.blurb: I found a world that is not in the Directory. It has people on it. They are well. They have no gods, no monsters, and no word for why. This is the shortest entry I have ever filed.

entries.title: Why We Measure Time In Hells
entries.phenomenon: Every date in Galactic Standard is written in units named after afterlives
entries.blurb: Four hundred entries of filing complaints about a conversion table that does not multiply out. I finally went and asked in person. The error is not an error. It is a headstone.

entries.title: The Second Chair
entries.planet: [none. A wooden case, wherever I happen to be sitting.]
entries.phenomenon: A case with ninety-one slots, built badly, on purpose.
entries.blurb: I bought wood, I borrowed a number I did not earn, and I wrote down the first thing that has never been on file anywhere: a man nine decks down and what he eats for breakfast.

entries.title: The Weather They Made Up
entries.phenomenon: A family that has maintained a rain which does not exist for nine generations
entries.blurb: On a Concluded world where nobody wonders about anything any more, one family still waits for a rain that was never real, and their children are the only children on the planet who ask why.

entries.title: The Cold Case Of All Fourteen
entries.phenomenon: All fourteen gods and all fourteen monsters of Dhurin died in the same night, four thousand clicks ago, and the Directory file on it has never closed
entries.blurb: A civilisation of detectives hands an outsider their oldest cold case: twenty eight murders, one night, no suspects, four thousand clicks unsolved. I got close enough to the answer that I wish I hadn't.

entries.title: The Last Thing He Taught Them
entries.phenomenon: A planet's axial wander corrected by a god who trained his own replacements and ran out of time by exactly one lesson
entries.blurb: A god announced the hour he would stop, three hundred clicks out, and spent every one of them teaching a room full of people to do his job. They finished the syllabus. They did not finish in time.

entries.title: What You Have Not Said Out Loud
entries.phenomenon: Every Ovai narrates what they feel, in full and out loud, to whoever is nearest, continuously, as a matter of survival
entries.blurb: On Threnn a thing can only hurt you if you have not said it out loud, so they say everything, immediately, to whoever is near. They noticed I was not doing that. I left anyway.

entries.title: The Weight Of The Case
entries.phenomenon: A case that weighs more than the sum of its own empty weight and its own pages, by a small and growing margin
entries.blurb: I weighed the case. Then I weighed the pages. Then I weighed the case with nothing in it. The numbers do not add up the way numbers are supposed to, and I have decided the honest thing to do about that is write down the numbers and nothing else.

entries.title: Six Worlds, Six Fences
entries.phenomenon: Six standing bearings, plotted as real lines from each world's own position instead of as directions, land on each other in pairs
entries.blurb: I promised to keep measuring and report the result either way. I reported a negative from Entry #2300. It was true and it was not the whole answer, and Ossul owns a sewing kit that proved it.

entries.title: The One That Stayed Open
entries.phenomenon: A calendar that is knowingly, deliberately, and permanently wrong
entries.blurb: One world pulled back from Concluded. They did it by breaking their own calendar on purpose and forbidding anyone, ever, from fixing it. I met the woman who explains why, and I still cannot tell you if she is right.

entries.title: Someone Has Been Reading
entries.planet: [none. Aboard ship, nineteen days out from anywhere, exactly where nobody could have gotten in.]
entries.phenomenon: A set of measurements, corrected in a hand that is not his own, inside a case nobody could have reached.
entries.blurb: Somebody went through my measurements in a hand that is not mine and got them more right than I did, and by the time I had ruled out everybody it could have been, there was only one thing left standing, and it was the thing I built.

entries.title: The Back Of The Case
entries.planet: [none. Deep Registry, nine decks down, and the back of a wooden case.]
entries.phenomenon: A Standard Interval assigned a length for the first time since the Directory's founding, sitting beside one that still has none
entries.blurb: I wrote the last page of this case eighty-one pages before I had any right to reach it, and put the one word I have refused all season somewhere it will never be spoken aloud again. Then I went and found out a unit of time has been assigned a length for the first time since the Directory was founded, and nobody will say why.

worlds.d: Nine days of tide, still owed
A count of eleven, still running
Four billion graves, each one aimed
A ring about the size of a small moon
Concluded. Kept open by a lie.
The only open file in the sky
Only the unsaid can reach you
A calendar kept wrong on purpose
Designation withheld. Concluded. A Hellheim was keyed to its year, and the only surviving record of that year is a conversion error nobody has corrected.
